title: Coordinate-normalized Dolbeault sheaf data on a varying-dimensional analytic atlas
statement: Let $M$ be a topological space with a finite-dimensional complex analytic atlas $A$, with dimension allowed to vary, as in [def-sfb-smooth-analytic-data]. For an open $U$, a coordinate tensor family assigns a complex-valued continuous real alternating $k$-tensor at each point of $U$ in each chart, for every $k\geq0$. A smooth family has real $C^\infty$ coefficients in charts and satisfies the cotangent pullback law under the complex Jacobian of each transition map. It has integer type $(p,q)$ if it is zero outside exterior degree $p+q$ and outside $0\leq p,q\leq n$ in an $n$-dimensional chart, and the sum of insertion of $Jv=iv$ in its arguments is multiplication by $i(p-q)$. A holomorphic $p$-form is a smooth type-$(p,0)$ family whose coordinate tensor coefficients are complex analytic. Dolbeault sheaf data consist of sheaves $\mathcal A^{p,q}$ and $\Omega^p$ of complex vector spaces [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with injective evaluations whose ranges are exactly these respective families and which preserve linear combinations and restrictions; the inclusion $\Omega^p\to\mathcal A^{p,0}$ is the identity on these tensors. The sheaf morphisms $\bar\partial:\mathcal A^{p,q}\to\mathcal A^{p,q+1}$ and $\partial:\mathcal A^{p,q}\to\mathcal A^{p+1,q}$ are normalized by requiring their sum to be the ordinary real coordinate exterior derivative. The holomorphic derivative $d_{\mathrm{hol}}:\Omega^0\to\Omega^1$ is normalized by the complex derivative of the coordinate scalar function. These are presentations by all sections and maps; square-zero identities, resolution exactness, and cohomological vanishing are not assumed. Global sections is evaluation on $M$, in this complex coefficient category, and its higher cohomology means the right derived functors of this evaluation [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. A universe lift of the complex coefficient field is understood via its canonical ring equivalence with $\mathbf C$.

lean.statement: structure DolbeaultSheafData {M : Type u} [TopologicalSpace M] (A : Atlas M)
lean.note: A sectionwise, Jacobian-normalized presentation on the existing varying-dimension Atlas. Smooth and holomorphic tensors have exact range conditions and restriction laws. The lifted complex coefficient field is canonically the usual complex field; the lift aligns the site and module universes. No sheaf, map or differential is chosen from an existence theorem, and no exactness or vanishing is included in the definition.
